later_packages.notes: Closes the term-level identity recorded as the remaining obligation in N34/TermIdentityFinal and adds the corrected formula-level code substitution (fixing the double-encoded `all` shadow branch of CodeStoreFixF). Does NOT change the gated status of ERCF-3: no proof-predicate representability, no reflection, no diagonal fixed point.

Checks the decodability/injectivity obligation recorded as deliberately unformalised in ObjectSyntax: the concrete codeT/codeF are not injective (var 2 and num 0 collide), with a numeral-fragment positive control. Does NOT provide a repaired coding and does NOT change the gated status of ERCF-3.

Fixes what a coding repair must provide (C-164 roundtrip ⇒ injectivity), gives the structured tree coding as decodable positive control (C-163), and derives that the current Nat coding admits no decoder (C-165). Does NOT provide a Nat-valued repaired coding; ERCF-3 stays gated.

First piece of the arithmetic half of the coding repair: double/odd tag disjointness (double injective, double n != odd m), the var/num fragment coder codeAtom (2n / 2n+1) is the first Nat-valued injective coding in the chain, and the *function* `double` misses 1 so the avar-only fragment is not surjective. [CORRECTED 2026-09-13 by the independent-audit absorption: the original note attributed the non-surjectivity to `codeAtom`, but the machine-checked lemma `one-has-no-preimage` is about `double`, and `codeAtom` is in fact surjective (see MP-ERCF3-T3-C168-COUNTERCHECK-001 / claims C-184-C-185). The default branch of the later full decoders is justified by `codeT'`/`codeF'` themselves: their bit lists are non-empty, so 1 is not in their image. The application node and the decoder remain open.]

Bit-level substrate of the arithmetic half of the coding repair: least-significant-bit extraction and halving (parity/half/twice), the bundling code codeBits with its extraction lemma pair, the round-trip on a bit list whose length is supplied, and the bound that the code dominates its own length (so a future parser can take its fuel from the code itself). The symbol layer (self-delimiting var/num index bits and constructor tags), the parser with its default branch and the round-trip on the image remain open.

Closes the coding-repair obligation of CodingRepair (C-163/C-164/C-165) at the coding layer: the self-delimiting unary index layer, the symbol layer (two tag bits for var/num plus their index, one tag bit for application) with a streaming parser whose round trip is fuel-exact (a frame stack solves sequential consumption while terminating structurally on the fuel), the length/bound/extra-fuel bookkeeping, and finally the repaired coder codeT' = codeBits . bits with a total decoder dec (default branches included) and round trip dec (codeT' t) = t, hence injectivity by C-164. Only Tm coding/decoding is covered: the proof predicate P, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open and ERCF-3 stays gated.

Lifts the repaired coding from Tm (C-176) to Fml, which is the layer the diagonal machinery actually quotes. The formula symbol layer (two tag bits for =f/bot/=>f, plus the binder index of all) comes with a streaming parser whose round trip is exact in the iteration count; the Tm children of =f are handed to the term-level parser as a black box (fuel = the length of the remaining bit list); the length bound STEPS <= LEN makes the repaired formula code its own fuel; and codeF' = codeBits . bitsF comes with a total decoder decF and the round trip decF (codeF' phi) = phi, hence injectivity. Only Fml coding/decoding is covered: formula-layer substitution alignment, proof-predicate representability, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open, and ERCF-3 stays gated.

Substitution and quotation over the repaired coding. With a decoder in hand, code-level substitution can be defined as decode-substitute-encode, and the agreement with syntax-level substitution becomes a corollary: substCodeT k n (codeT' t) = codeT' (substT k n t) and substCodeF k n (codeF' phi) = codeF' (substF k n phi). Quotation (the numeral of the repaired formula code) is injective, and the diagonal instance is a substitution instance of the same formula whose code is reached by the code-level substitution. Honest boundary: these code-level functions are defined through the decoder, so nothing here claims that the object theory can represent them -- representability, reflection and the diagonal fixed point remain open and ERCF-3 stays gated.

Replays the independent audit's countercheck inside this repo, with the complete transitive import closure pinned: codeAtom (anum zero) = 1 has an explicit preimage (C-184) and codeAtom is surjective (C-185). Import origin: audit/imports/audit-c168-20260913/.

Replacement justification for the default branches after the C-168 narrative was withdrawn: the repaired coders miss 1, so a total decoder must decide what to do on non-codes and the default branch is reachable. C-186: (t : Tm) -> codeT' t != 1. C-187: (phi : Fml) -> codeF' phi != 1. Proof route: any bit list here is non-empty, codeBits (b :: bs) = pack b (codeBits bs), and pack b c >= 2 whenever c >= 1 (C-172 supplies the remaining bundle >= 1).

later_packages_policy: Additive registry for proof packages that entered the project after the frozen d3dfb0e snapshot. The frozen 17-package receipt is never rewritten; each later entry is checked for Git-tracked source/toolchain/run files and a run receipt whose index status is INDEXED_IN_CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX with exit code 0.
frozen_row_policy: Proof and claim rows retain their run-time indexed status text. Current Git closure is an orthogonal registry so historical index-row manifests remain valid under append-only evolution.
scope: Version closure proves recoverability of the listed project assets at the exact commit. It does not expand any theorem, certify originality/model understanding, or turn source-inspected no-global-choice into a replayed claim.
